text:
maria: RFC follow-up — continuous scheduler: cohort-fence shim vs slot-level ownership. TL;DR: which path reduces tail latency without a massive refactor?

devin: If we merge the cohort-fence shim we get faster iteration. But it adds an intermediate lease layer; could mask root cause.

jena: Concern: shim increases enqueued-set complexity, eviction harder. We saw starvation in sim when tenant distribution is skewed.

alex: slot ownership removes late-join amplification, but it's a big change across allocator + kvcache + placement. Not trivial.

maria: Agree. Tradeoffs: shim = lower dev cost, incremental rollout, easier rollback, easier telemetry. slot ownership = stronger isolation, less jitter, lower worst-case tails.

devin: Can we do a hybrid? cohorts for bursty tenants, slots for heavy steady tenants. Policy routing picks based on observed QPS/variance.

priya: Hybrid means routing decisions + admission tags. That complexity pushes responsibility into admission API and the router. Need a clear interface.

alex: Also consider rollback story: shim is easy to flip off. Slot ownership requires migrating placement state and a multi-stage rollout.

jena: On preemption: slots simplifies preempt handoff and makes evictions deterministic. Shim requires refining partial-eviction rules and can cause reordering in the batcher.

maria: Proposed next step: prototype the shim with guardrails (tight eviction heuristics, headroom signals) and run canary. Collect 50th/95th/99.9th latencies + kv-cache hit rate.

scheduler-bot: experiment created: cohort-fence-shim-canary — target: hostpool-3 — start ETA 30m — tracking: /experiments/CF-shim-canary-1715009990

devin: Tests to run: synthetic bursty workload (many small reqs), steady heavy tenant, KV-miss sequences, admission spike during GC. Also chaos: node drain during steady load.

priya: Telemetry checklist: per-cohort headroom gauge, eviction_count, late_join_rate, batch_size_histogram, batcher_span tags for cohort/slot. Add alerts on rising late_join_rate or eviction spikes.

alex: If the canary shows persistent tail regens or starvation we escalate to the slot-ownership plan. Tentative timeline for slot ownership prototyping: 6 weeks.

maria: Action items: (1) Devin + Jena land shim prototype behind a feature flag; (2) Priya add the telemetry and dashboards; (3) Alex write a slot-ownership sketch + migration plan.

devin: I'll open the PR with flag + a tiny e2e harness. Requesting reviewers: @maria @alex.

jena: I'll add an experiment doc template capturing test vectors and known edge cases (late-join, evict cascade, kv-cache warming).

maria: Thanks all. We'll reconvene after the canary runs and share metrics in the eng-runtime weekly. :thumbsup:
